newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Illovo eyes Lonrho, other sugar investments.
newsitem.headline: Illovo eyes Lonrho, other sugar investments.

text.p: South Africa's Illovo Sugar Ltd said on Thursday it was evaluating potential new investments in the rest of Africa, including Lonrho Sugar.
The sugar division of Britain's Lonrho Plc, with operations in South Africa, Mauritius, Malawi and Swaziland, is widely expected to be sold as part of the group's unbundling.
In addition to Lonrho Sugar, Illovo said it was also interested in the privatisation of the sugar industries in Kenya and Ivory Coast.

The company said in its interim results for the six months to March 31, 1997 that the rehabilitation of the sugar mill and estates at Maragra in Mozambique -- in which Illovo held a 50 percent stake -- had commenced.
The first sugar production at Maragra was expected in July 1998.
Illovo said sugar production for the 1996/97 season increased by 189,362 tonnes to a company record of 995,136 tonnes.
This equated to 44 percent of total South African sugar industry production, the company said.
